skill.name: ffmpeg
skill.description: Video and audio processing with FFmpeg. Use for format conversion, resizing, compression, audio extraction, and preparing assets for Remotion. Triggers include converting GIF to MP4, resizing video, extracting audio, compressing files, or any media transformation task.
skill.summary: Practical FFmpeg command patterns for converting, editing, compressing, and preparing media assets.
skill.author: digitalsamba

security_audit.summary: All 63 static findings are false positives because they match Markdown examples, shell syntax, or a troubleshooting table rather than hidden execution or reconnaissance. The skill documents local FFmpeg workflows and shows no prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Documented shell commands accept input and output paths supplied by the user.
remediation.suggestion: When implementing these examples, pass arguments as an array or quote and validate paths; do not construct shell commands from untrusted strings.

remediation.issue: The batch conversion example derives output names from asset filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the filename expansion quoted, reject path traversal, and restrict the input glob to an intended asset directory.

remediation.issue: FFmpeg processes media files that may be malformed or resource-intensive.
remediation.suggestion: Run processing with resource limits and a non-privileged account when handling untrusted media.

content.user_title: Process Video and Audio with FFmpeg
content.value_statement: Media workflows often need reliable conversion, resizing, compression, and timing adjustments across formats. This skill provides practical FFmpeg commands for preparing media assets and Remotion inputs.
actual_capabilities: Convert video, audio, and GIF files between common formats.
Resize, crop, pad, compress, and optimize video for web platforms.
Extract audio and adjust audio codecs, bitrate, volume, and speed.
Trim clips, change playback speed, add fades, and concatenate compatible videos.
Prepare rendered media for Remotion and platform-specific delivery.
limitations: The skill provides command guidance and does not install FFmpeg or codecs.
Commands require valid input files, supported codecs, and sufficient disk space.
Platform limits and codec support can change, so verify current publishing requirements.
Complex filter graphs may require testing against the specific media source.

use_cases.title: Prepare Remotion Assets
use_cases.description: Convert recordings, GIFs, and source clips into reliable assets for Remotion compositions.

use_cases.title: Optimize Published Video
use_cases.description: Create platform-specific exports with suitable resolution, codecs, bitrate, and fast-start metadata.

use_cases.title: Automate Media Operations
use_cases.description: Build repeatable shell workflows for batch conversion, audio extraction, trimming, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Media File
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my input file to a browser-compatible MP4. Preserve the aspect ratio, use broadly supported video and audio codecs, and explain the command.

prompt_templates.title: Resize for Web
prompt_templates.prompt: Resize this video to fit [width] by [height] while preserving its aspect ratio. Add padding or cropping as appropriate and recommend output settings.

prompt_templates.title: Match a Scene Duration
prompt_templates.prompt: Make [input file] fit a [target duration]-second Remotion scene. Keep video and audio synchronized, show the speed calculation, and provide the FFmpeg command.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Platform Export Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable FFmpeg export workflow for YouTube, a short-form vertical platform, and a website embed. Include codecs, scaling, bitrate or quality settings, validation commands, and input-path safety guidance.

output_examples.input: Convert a 30-second GIF into a web-ready MP4.
output_examples.output: A concise FFmpeg command that converts the GIF, forces even dimensions, uses a compatible pixel format, and places metadata for progressive playback.

output_examples.input: Fit a 60-second demo into a 20-second scene with synchronized audio.
output_examples.output: A command using a three-times video speed adjustment and matching audio tempo, with a short explanation of the timing calculation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a rendered video for a website embed.
output: A web-oriented export with scaled dimensions, H.264 video, AAC audio, and fast-start metadata.
A validation step that reports the resulting video codec.

best_practices: State the input, output, target dimensions, and required audio behavior before choosing filters.
Use re-encoding when accurate trimming or synchronized speed changes matter.
Validate output codec, duration, dimensions, and playback before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not assume stream copy produces frame-accurate cuts at arbitrary timestamps.
Do not build shell commands by concatenating untrusted paths or filenames.
Do not use one export profile for every platform without checking its limits.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers common FFmpeg workflows for video and audio conversion, editing, compression, validation, and Remotion preparation.

faq.question: Does it install FFmpeg?
faq.answer: No. FFmpeg and the required encoders must already be installed in the environment.

faq.question: Can it convert GIF files to MP4?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a browser-compatible GIF-to-MP4 pattern with even dimensions and fast-start metadata.

faq.question: Can it keep audio synchronized when changing speed?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses matching video timestamp and audio tempo filters, including chained filters for higher speeds.

faq.question: Can it prepare files for social platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example settings for YouTube, Twitter or X, LinkedIn, websites, and preview GIFs.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted media?
faq.answer: Use a non-privileged process with resource limits, validate paths, and keep shell arguments quoted when processing untrusted files.
